title: Eating out with friends
goal: Order for a group at a restaurant or teahouse, talk about the dishes you love, say what you feel like eating, complain that it's too spicy or not salty enough, and win (or lose) the fight over the bill.
intro:
Eating out with Pashtun friends is loud, generous and long: a heap of chapli kebabs in Peshawar, karahi by the kilo at Namak Mandi, Kabuli palaw and mantu in Kabul, endless green tea in a چايخانه. Someone orders for the whole table, everyone pushes food onto everyone else's plate, and then comes the best part — the argument over who pays.

This unit gives you the dishes and the table talk. The grammar is **too / enough / a little** (Pashto's ډېر does double duty for 'very' and 'too') and the lovely **زړه مې … غواړي** — 'my heart wants…' — for 'I feel like…'.

m. آرډر ورکول 'to order'. In Kabul also فرمايش.
m. The pride of Peshawar and Charsadda.

vocab.en: karahi (meat cooked in a wok, sold by the kilo)

vocab.note: f. Filled with potato or leek (ګندنه).
f. The green one is mint and coriander.
f. In Kabul eaten with fried fish in winter.
f. له لوږې مړ شوم 'I'm starving'.
f. اشتها مې نشته 'I'm not hungry'.
m pl. غوړي يې ډېر دي 'it's too oily'.
f: پخه. pl: پاخه (m), پخې (f). Opposite: اوم 'raw'.
m. زما وار دی 'it's my turn'.

phrases.en: How many of you are there?
I feel like a chapli kebab.
I'm starving! (lit. I died of hunger)
I'm not hungry. (lit. I have no appetite)
It needs more salt. (lit. its salt is little)

grammar.title: Too, enough, a little
grammar.body:
**Too.** Pashto doesn't separate 'very' and 'too': **ډېر** does both, and the context — or your face — makes it clear: دا **ډېر** تېز دی 'this is very / too spicy'. To make *too* unmistakable:
- **ډېر زيات** 'far too much': مرچ يې **ډېر زيات** دي 'it's far too spicy (lit. its chillies are too many)'.
- **دومره … چې** 'so … that': **دومره** تېز دی **چې** نه شم خوړلای 'it's so spicy I can't eat it'.
- Pashto likes to say what the food *has*, with **يې** 'its': مالګه يې **زياته** ده 'it's too salty', غوړي يې **ډېر** دي 'it's too oily'.

**Not enough.** Name what's missing and call it **کم** 'little': مالګه يې **کمه** ده 'it needs more salt', ډوډۍ **کمه** ده 'there isn't enough bread'.

**Enough.** **پوره** 'enough' (ډوډۍ **پوره** ده 'there's enough food'), and to stop someone filling your plate: **بس!** or **بس دی!** 'that's enough!'.

**A little, a bit more.** **لږ** 'a little' (لږ مرچ 'a little chilli'), **لږ نور** 'a bit more', and لږ + verb for 'go easy on': مرچ **لږ** واچوه 'go easy on the chilli'.

The trap: کم، زيات and the taste words are adjectives, so they agree with the noun: مالګه (f) **کمه** · غوړي (m pl) **زيات** · اوبه (f pl) **کمې** · کړايي (f) **تېزه** · کباب (m) **تېز**.

grammar.title: I feel like …: زړه مې … غواړي
grammar.body:
To say what you're in the mood for, Pashto says **'my heart wants'**: **زړه مې … غواړي**. The heart (زړه) is the subject, so the verb is always 3rd person **غواړي**, and 'my, your, his' is a clitic right after زړه:

زړه **مې** کباب غواړي 'I feel like kebab' · زړه **دې** څه غواړي؟ 'what do you feel like?' · زړه **يې** چای غواړي 'he / she fancies some tea' · زړه **مو** څه غواړي؟ 'what do you (all) feel like?'

To feel like *doing* something, add **چې** + the perfective subjunctive: زړه مې غواړي **چې** نن بهر ډوډۍ **وخورو** 'I feel like eating out today'.

**Negative:** زړه مې **نه** غواړي 'I don't feel like it'. **Past:** زړه مې **غوښتل** چې … 'I felt like …'.

Related: **وږی يم** 'I'm hungry', **له لوږې مړ شوم** 'I'm starving', **اشتها مې نشته** 'I've no appetite', **موړ شوم** 'I'm full'.

The trap: it's the heart that wants, not you — never زه زړه غواړم or زړه مې غواړم.

examples.en: I feel like eating out today.

lines.native: ورور جانه، حساب راوړه… نن زما په حساب!

lines.native: نه ياره، هېڅکله! پرون هم تا پيسې ورکړې. نيم نيم کوو.
lines.roman: na yā́ra, hetskə́la! parún ham tā páyse wárkṛe. nim nim kawú.
lines.en: No way, man! You paid yesterday too. Let's split it.

lines.native: ګوره، که ما ته پيسې راکړې، خفه به شم!
lines.roman: góra, ka mā ta páyse rā́kṛe, xapá ba shəm!
lines.en: Look, if you give me money, I'll be offended!

lines.speaker: Jawad
lines.native: ښه، نو بله ورځ زما وار دی.
lines.roman: ṣə, no bə́la wradz zmā wār day.
lines.en: Fine — then next time it's my turn.

culture: Among Pashtuns, whoever suggests the meal usually pays — and everyone else is expected to protest. The fight over the bill (grabbing it, slipping money to the waiter, swearing 'والله زه يې ورکوم!') is a ritual; insist a couple of times, then accept gracefully and say **بله ورځ زما وار دی**. Students and colleagues do split (**نيم نيم**, or each pays **خپله برخه**), but it's still said with a little apology. At the table the host keeps loading your plate — say **بس دی، مننه** two or three times, and leave a little food to show you're full. Bread is torn by hand and used to scoop; eat with your right hand. In Peshawar, go for chapli kebab (Charsadda style), tikka and karahi by the kilo at Namak Mandi, and pakoras and samosas at tea time; in Kabul, Kabuli palaw, mantu, ashak and bolani, and in winter the famous fried fish with jalebi. Most restaurants have a separate **family hall** for women and families. Tea is green (شين چای) after a heavy meal, often with sugared almonds or sweets; in Peshawar milky black tea is just as common.

tip.title: Ordering for the table
tip.body:
- The waiter asks **څو تنه ياست؟** — answer **درې تنه** (تن 'person' + counting -ه).
- Order with **راوړه** 'bring': دوه چای راوړه. Polite: راوړئ.
- Call the waiter **ورور جانه** 'brother' or, to an older man, **کاکا** — never 'waiter'.

tip.title: زړه مې … غواړي — I feel like …
tip.body:
- 'My heart wants': **زړه مې** چای **غواړي** 'I fancy some tea'.
- The verb is always **غواړي** (the heart wants); the clitic shows whose heart: مې، دې، يې، مو.
- Doing something: زړه مې غواړي **چې** … + perfective: چې بهر **لاړ شو**.
- Not زه زړه غواړم!
tip.pattern: زړه + مې / دې / يې / مو + … + غواړي

tip.title: Too much, not enough
tip.body:
- **ډېر** = very *or* too; **ډېر زيات** = far too much; **دومره … چې** = so … that.
- Say what the food has: مالګه يې **زياته** ده 'too salty' · مالګه يې **کمه** ده 'not salty enough'.
- **لږ** a little · **لږ نور** a bit more · **بس!** enough!
- These words agree: مالګه **کمه** (f) · غوړي **زيات** (m pl) · کباب **تېز** (m).
tip.pattern: … يې زيات / کم + دی / ده / دي

tip.title: The fight over the bill
tip.body:
- Whoever invites pays: **نن زما په حساب** 'today it's on me'.
- Everyone protests — insist a couple of times, then give in: **بله ورځ زما وار دی** 'next time it's my turn'.
- Students split: **نيم نيم** or each pays **خپله برخه**.
- At the table, stop more food coming with **بس دی، مننه**.
